summary: POP3 module is the most feature-complete of the tranche: T1 posture (STLS, plaintext USER/PASS accepted, CAPA/IMPLEMENTATION disclosure), T2 offline-crackable material (APOP challenge, CRAM/DIGEST challenges captured), T2 NTLM Type-2 AV_PAIR harvest (actually parses NetBIOS/DNS/domain), T2 USER-differential enum, and T3 credentialed mailbox read (STAT/LIST/UIDL/TOP + address+Received-from harvest). Login-delay aware spray helper implemented but analyze() never calls it — biggest gap: the spray path is dead code unless the operator supplies creds directly. Also missing: cross-service wire (no known_mail_accounts feed for POP3-enumerated users), and no APOP-response cracking (only challenge captured).

findings.tier_evidence: CAPA IMPLEMENTATION field disclosure — fingerprint only.
findings.tester_next_step: nc IP 110 ; CAPA ; note IMPLEMENTATION line and cross-check offline CVE DB

findings.title_pattern: POP3 APOP timestamp discloses internal hostname/domain
findings.tier_evidence: APOP timestamp '<pid.time@host>' parsed from greeting — the @host suffix IS internal FQDN leakage, not just a fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire into known_hostnames + known_domains so downstream DNS/AD/web tools consume it.
findings.tester_next_step: nc IP 110 ; note @hostname in first line ; add to /etc/hosts or feed the AD reader for cross-service correlation

findings.tier_evidence: Server actively advertises the crackable challenge; a captured client response completes the offline crack tuple — the challenge half is proven in hand.
findings.promotion_notes: Add tcpdump/MITM helper doc + hashcat launch template using the captured timestamp; not something recce automates in-band.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -A 'tcp port 110 and host IP' during real login ; then hashcat with format <md5>:<timestamp> mode 11500-style ; rockyou.txt is enough for most.

findings.title_pattern: POP3 does not offer STLS on 110/tcp
findings.tier_evidence: CAPA absence of STLS token — posture-only flag.
findings.promotion_notes: Not promotable inside recce; motivates the sniffing playbook.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -A 'tcp port 110 and host IP' to capture live USER/PASS

findings.title_pattern: POP3 accepts USER/PASS in cleartext (no STLS enforced)
findings.tier_evidence: USER + PASS with bogus creds was processed rather than refused with a TLS-required -ERR — deterministic proof that the plaintext auth path is live.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain the login-delay-aware spray() (already implemented, but not called from analyze) against USER-enumerated names for T3 mailbox access.
findings.tester_next_step: hydra -L users.txt -P rockyou.txt pop3://IP:110 -t 2 -w 5 (respect any LOGIN-DELAY seen in CAPA)

findings.title_pattern: POP3 SASL PLAIN/LOGIN still offered inside TLS
findings.tier_evidence: Compared pre-TLS and post-TLS CAPA and observed the plaintext mech set is unchanged — a determinable protocol misconfig (RFC 2595 §4).
findings.promotion_notes: Posture finding; no exploit escalation beyond the sniffing narrative.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -starttls pop3 -connect IP:110 ; type CAPA post-TLS — note PLAIN/LOGIN still present

findings.title_pattern: POP3 weak SASL mechanism advertised: <MECH> / CRAM-MD5 challenge captured
findings.tier_evidence: Weak-SASL advertisement is T0 fingerprint; the CRAM-MD5 / DIGEST-MD5 branch actively captures the challenge on demand — promoting the finding kind to T2 (offline-crackable material in hand). Severity high covers PLAIN/LOGIN/NTLM/GSSAPI/ANONYMOUS variants.
findings.promotion_notes: Combine captured challenge with an MITM-sniffed real client response — offline crack lands a working credential.
findings.tester_next_step: For CRAM-MD5: hashcat -m 10200 <b64_chal>:<b64_resp> rockyou.txt after capturing a real client's AUTH CRAM-MD5 response.

findings.title_pattern: POP3 AUTH NTLM Type-2 leaks NetBIOS/DNS names
findings.tier_evidence: Real NTLM Type-1 sent and Type-2 parsed for AV_PAIRs (nb_computer, nb_domain, dns_computer, dns_domain, dns_tree) — a concrete pre-auth information-disclosure primitive, not just an advertisement.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire nb_domain + dns_domain into known_domains and dns_computer into known_hostnames so subsequent AD/web tools consume them; use domain as the AD anchor for RID cycling / kerbrute.

findings.tier_evidence: Cert CN/SAN grab + verify-error detection — posture flag.
findings.promotion_notes: Names in the cert already seed known_hostnames via the caller — real exploitation requires active MITM (out-of-band).
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:995 ; grab CN/SAN; use in mitmproxy --certs to MITM a client that doesn't verify.

findings.tier_evidence: Regex match against banner/IMPLEMENTATION — version-gated CVE claim only.
findings.promotion_notes: For CVE-2019-11500: send an oversized IMAP/POP3 command to trigger the OOB write and observe memory-disclosure fragments in the response.
findings.tester_next_step: Confirm exact build (CAPA IMPLEMENTATION), then check https://dovecot.org/security.html for the exact CVE; do NOT fire memory-corruption PoC without ROE.

findings.title_pattern: POP3 valid usernames enumerated via USER-command differential
findings.tier_evidence: Multi-connection USER differential returns concrete existing account names (majority-vs-outlier response line + timing) — proven-existing accounts, not fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire the harvested list into known_mail_accounts (imap.py already does; pop3.py analyze does NOT) and chain into spray() honoring LOGIN-DELAY for a t3 mailbox foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: hydra -L pop3_enum_users.txt -P rockyou.txt pop3://IP:110 -t 2 -w <LOGIN-DELAY+1> ; add -e nsr.

findings.tier_evidence: STAT/LIST/UIDL/TOP against a live authenticated session, actually pulling and parsing message headers + harvesting addresses / Received-from hosts — an authenticated foothold with returned loot.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire the harvested From:/To:/Received: hosts into known_users, known_hostnames, known_domains for cross-service pivots. Optionally add RETR of top-N messages for full-body loot.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 -c 'import poplib; p=poplib.POP3_SSL("IP"); p.user(u); p.pass_(pw); print(p.stat()); print(p.list()); print(p.top(1,25))' ; feed addresses to smtp + AD reader.

findings.title_pattern: POP3 weak / default credentials confirmed by spray
findings.tier_evidence: Fires ONLY when the credentialed pass landed with the default_creds flag — but note: analyze() never sets used_defaults=True (the pop3 module has no default-spray path, only operator-supplied creds). Dead-code branch as currently wired.
findings.promotion_notes: Implement a bounded default-spray (mirror imap._spray_defaults) that honors LOGIN-DELAY via the existing spray() helper. Would then actually fire.
findings.tester_next_step: Add pop3 spray of default set (admin/admin, mail/mail, cyrus/cyrus, postmaster/postmaster) — until then, run manually: hydra -C /usr/share/wordlists/seclists/Passwords/Default-Credentials/default-passwords.txt pop3://IP
